# Temple Scroll Column 14 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 14 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 14:1 — "sons of the herd" vs. "from the herd" — bull description

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "twelve young bulls, sons of the herd" | Literal bene bakar |
| LOGOS | "twelve young bulls from the herd" | "From the herd" is standard English; bene here means "of the class of" |
| PNEUMA | "twelve young bulls" | Omits "of the herd" entirely as redundant |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "From the herd" adequately conveys the Hebrew without the Hebraism "sons of the herd." PNEUMA's omission loses information, as bene bakar distinguishes domestic cattle from other bovines.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 14:3 — "perpetual burnt offering" vs. "regular daily burnt offering" — olat ha-tamid

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the perpetual burnt offering" | Literal olat ha-tamid |
| LOGOS | "the perpetual burnt offering" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the regular daily burnt offering" | "Regular daily" clarifies that tamid means the twice-daily offering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "perpetual burnt offering" (EMET/LOGOS). While PNEUMA's "regular daily" is descriptively accurate, tamid means "perpetual/continual" and the standard rendering should be preserved. The twice-daily schedule is not stated in tamid itself.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 14:13 — "vow offerings" vs. "votive offerings" vs. "vow offerings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your vow offerings" | Literal nidreikhem |
| LOGOS | "your votive offerings" | "Votive" is the standard scholarly adjective |
| PNEUMA | "whatever vow offerings you bring" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "votive offerings" (LOGOS). "Votive" is the established English term for offerings made in fulfillment of a vow, used consistently in biblical scholarship. EMET's "vow offerings" is acceptable but less precise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 14:14 — "peace offerings" vs. "fellowship offerings" — shelamim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your peace offerings" | Traditional rendering of shelamim |
| LOGOS | "peace offerings" | Standard in most major translations |
| PNEUMA | "fellowship offerings" | Captures the communal eating aspect of shelamim |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "peace offerings" (EMET/LOGOS), consistent with the project's established convention from Leviticus (shelamim = "peace offerings"). PNEUMA's "fellowship offerings" is the NIV rendering but introduces inconsistency with the project's existing Leviticus translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Consistent with project convention.

---
